results.summary_before: The project generates a pseudo-random soundtrack via PWM and displays a waveform on a VGA monitor.
results.summary: This demoscene competition entry generates a pseudo-random soundtrack via PWM and displays a waveform on a VGA monitor. It uses the Tiny VGA Pmod on uo_out and Mike's audio Pmod on uio_out[7]. The design is written in Verilog and runs from a 50 MHz clock with asynchronous reset. A silicon test report confirms the design is working.

results.summary_before: This combinational design implements a 3-bit ALU supporting subtraction, addition, XOR, and AND, with its output routed to both an octal decoder and a Gray code decoder for display on two 7-segment displays. A selector chooses the ALU operation and another selects whether the octal or Gray decoder drives the displays, with the Gray decoder specially mapped to decimal for the displays. Testing requires setting the two 3-bit numbers and the selectors, then observing the result on the external displays. External hardware includes two common-cathode 7-segment displays, fourteen 330-ohm resistors, and a DC power source.

results.summary_before: This experiment implements a 512-bit shift register using D latches instead of flip-flops, with a single pulse rippling through the register to perform the shift.
results.summary: This experiment implements a 512-bit shift register using D latches instead of flip-flops, with a single pulse rippling through the register to perform the shift. It has one input, one output, and an edge-triggered control signal that updates the shift on either a rising or falling edge. Testing involves shifting zeros in until the register is empty, then shifting in a pattern and observing it appear on the output after 512 control transitions. No external hardware is required.

The documentation is sparse, with pin names all labeled '1', but the basic function is clear.
